description: [S7.4, kind `scope`] The cross-check (log/roadmap/S7/4_xcheck.py) drives the original only through body dispatches of live frames (P6 / H1, by frame-head count) plus frame 0's two modal clicks (title, location screen) through the harness's own screen waits and timing. A modal dispatch in a live frame (the F-key reports, the save dialog, the load browser: recordings `report`, `saveload`) is not driven: the app's dispatch log names the pump call only by its LivePump fields (kind, calls, cursor reads), not by the original pump function and caller, so it has no unambiguous point in the original. Only `hole` was cross-checked.
path to resolution: Have the live core report the pump function (the hooks.csv name tick calls) and its caller per pump call; post a modal batch at that function's entry with that return address, the n-th call since the previous batch.

description: [S7.4, kind `scope`] WM_RBUTTONDBLCLK is translated as rootWin_onPress2b (handler 11) then onPoint2, by analogy with the measured left button (onPress1b then onPoint, recording `hole` frame 100). onPress2b's body 0x00465840 is onPress1b's with the button word 0x00822d68 = 2, but no recording holds a right double click (a right click in the sandbox drops a tool or opens the radial menu, a modal loop U-1630 does not drive).
path to resolution: A right double click on a screen with no right-click action, cross-checked.

description: [S7.4, kind `value`] WM_MOUSEWHEEL (+120 and -120 at the in-game point (380, 290), recording `hole`) made no root-handler call in the original (no HANDLER record after its MSG) and left every sim object equal to the port's, which ignores the wheel. H1's PeekMessage range 0x200..0x20a (0x1006b801) includes 0x20a, so the wheel is dispatched there; what jgld's window procedure does with it beyond that was not traced. Other screens (lists, modal loops) are not measured.
path to resolution: Cross-check the wheel over a list box and the load browser.

description: [S7.4, kind `value`] The cursor the original reads in live frame f is answered from the app's frame-f CURSOR records (the k-th read gets the app's k-th read, later reads the last value). In 11 of the 340 frames of `hole` (run x5) the original read the cursor once more than the port (4 reads against 3): each is the frame where a WM_MOUSEMOVE or WM_MOUSEWHEEL was posted, which jgld's window procedure answers with its own read (U-1064, dropped by parse_trace); the original's and the app's cursor values are the same set in all 340 frames. In every frame of the recordings the app's reads in one frame have one value, so the extra read gets the same value; a cursor that changes between two reads of one frame would make the index mapping ambiguous.
path to resolution: Record the read's call site in the app's CURSOR records and serve by site.

description: [S7.4, kind `scope`] With `--keys message` the app's key table changes when the WINDOW thread receives a key message; the cross-check sets the original's virtual key when it POSTS the message at P6 / H1 of the dispatch's frame. The two agree for GetAsyncKeyState reads after P6 (mainLoop's body read is at mainLoop + 0xf10c, after H1) and for the handlers' own reads, which is what the recordings exercise (the driver keeps every modifier change 4 frames from the next input). A key message arriving between a frame's head and its P6 would change the app's answer for that frame's reads before P6 only. The real keyboard (`--keys system`, the default) is not cross-checked.
path to resolution: A recording with modifier changes in every frame phase; or have the host take the key table at the dispatch.

description: [S7.4, kind `scope`] The host's H1 rule (port/app/host.cpp: H1 takes the first queued mouse-class message only, as PeekMessage(0x200..0x20a) does) moves a mouse message ahead of key messages queued before it, so the app's handler order then differs from arrival order, as in the original. The recordings never queue a key and a mouse message together, so the reordering is unexercised; the live core's own replay is unaffected (the recording holds the order the host delivered).
path to resolution: A recording that posts a key and a click in one frame wait, cross-checked.

description: [S7.4, kind `scope`] The translator fixes the cross-check measured (modifier bits 0x10000 / 0x20000 / 0x40000 in the key-down's code and in the WM_CHAR's code, the double click's onPress1b) are in log/roadmap/S7/4_input_map.patch against S7.2's port/app/input_map.cpp and tools/input_check.cpp, applied only in S7.4's mirror. The corpus check (test_app_input, 16 passed) is unchanged because no corpus key-down has a modifier down and no corpus trace holds a double click.
path to resolution: The integrator applies the patch with S7.4's merge (4_merge.md).

description: [S7.4, kind `value`] g_frameMs (written at mainLoop + 0xf07f from H1's timeGetTime read, never read back: re/analysis/sim/time_model.md) is the only sim object that differs between the app's recording and the original's run (every record from record 1): the app answers real milliseconds from --clock-origin 0x100000, the original's virtual clock advances 1 ms per call and makes about 99 calls per frame. Every other sim object, g_seedTime and g_rng included, is equal in all records. Any later code that reads g_frameMs would break this.
path to resolution: None while g_frameMs stays write-only; a run whose app clock replays the original's per-frame clock counts would make it equal.
